title: Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol cont.: Bellarmine's mediate/immediate dodge — sufficient help for an Indian or American infant in the parents cannot be explained
pass_a_gloss: Secondly, Bellarmine is compelled to flee unto that distinction, mediate or immediate; nor does he dare to maintain that sufficient grace is immediately given unto all little ones. But how obscure this is — that unto this little one, born among the Indians or Americans, sufficient help was exhibited in his parents, when what sort this was, no one can explain! Further, if for the defense of sufficient grace it be lawful to flee unto ancestors, it is much safer and more certain to ascend even unto the first parents, concerning whom there is no question but that posterity also received sufficient grace in them, than to rest in any other of our ancestors whatsoever, concerning whom it will be uncertain whether they received such sufficient grace in the name of their children, or did not receive it.
pass_b_english: Second: Bellarmine is driven to the mediate-or-immediate distinction, and will not dare claim sufficient grace is given immediately to every infant. How dark that is — that an infant born among Indians or Americans had sufficient help shown in his parents, when no one can say what that help was! And if defending sufficient grace means fleeing to ancestors, it is far safer to go all the way back to the first parents — where no one doubts posterity also received sufficient grace in them — than to stop at any later ancestors, of whom it remains uncertain whether they received such sufficient grace in their children's name or not.
source_text: Secundo, Bellarminus cogitur confugere ad illam distinctionem, mediate vel immediate; nec audet sustinere sufficientem gratiam omnibus parvulis immediate dari. At quam hoc obscurum est, huic parvulo, inter Indos aut Americanos nato, in parentibus suis fuisse exhibitum auxilium sufficiens, cum quale hoc fuerit, nemo potest explicare! Porro, si ad defensionem sufficientis gratiae liceat ad majores confugere, multo tutius et certius est ad primos usque parentes ascendere, de quibus nulla quaestio est, quin sufficientem gratiam in illis et posteri acceperint, quam in aliis majoribus nostris quibuscunque subsistere, de quibus incertum erit acceperintne talem sufficientem gratiam filiorum suorum nomine, an non acceperint.
